q: 1. Venturimeter is used to
options: measure the velocity of a flowing liquid
measure the pressure of a flowing liquid
measure the discharge of liquid flowing in a pipe
measure the pressure difference of liquid flowing between two points
explain: A venturimeter is a standard device used to calculate the volume flow rate (discharge) in a pipeline.

q: 2. The velocity of the liquid flowing through the divergent portion of a venturimeter
explain: As the cross-sectional area increases in the divergent part, the velocity must decrease per the continuity equation.

q: 3. Coefficient of velocity is defined as the ratio of
options: actual velocity of jet at vena contracta to the theoretical velocity
area of jet at vena contracta to the area of orifice
actual discharge through an orifice to the theoretical discharge
explain: Cv = Actual Velocity / Theoretical Velocity. It accounts for losses due to friction.

q: 4. Coefficient of discharge Cd is equal to
explain: The overall discharge coefficient is the product of the contraction and velocity coefficients.

q: 5. An average value of coefficient of velocity is
explain: For a standard sharp-edged orifice, Cv typically ranges from 0.95 to 0.99.

q: 6. In an internal mouthpiece, if the jet after contraction does not touch the sides of the mouthpiece, then the mouthpiece is said to be
explain: When the jet discharges without wetting the internal walls, it is in a 'running free' condition.

q: 7. A notch is used to measure ............ of liquids.
explain: Notches and weirs are standard hydraulic structures used to measure the rate of flow (discharge) of liquids in open channels.

q: 8. If the coefficient of discharge is 0.6, then the discharge over a right angled notch is ............
explain: Plugging $C_d = 0.6$ into the V-notch formula $Q = \frac{8}{15} \times 0.6 	imes \sqrt{2 	imes 9.81} 	imes H^{5/2}$ results in approximately $1.417 H^{5/2}$.

q: 9. A structure used to dam up a stream or river over which the water flows is called ............
explain: While a dam holds water, a 'weir' is specifically the structure built across a river over which water flows for measurement or regulation.

q: 10. According to Francis formula, the discharge over a rectangular weir is ............
explain: Francis formula accounts for end contractions: $Q =  rac{2}{3} C_d (L - 0.1nH) \sqrt{2g} H^{3/2}$, where $n$ is the number of end contractions.

q: 11. The maximum discharge over a broad crested weir is ............
explain: The maximum discharge is $Q_{max} = 1.71 C_d L H^{3/2}$, derived using the critical depth condition.

q: 12. In a free nappe ............
options: the pressure below the nappe is atmospheric
the pressure below the nappe is negative
the pressure above the nappe is atmospheric
the pressure above the nappe is negative
explain: For a nappe to be 'free', air must circulate freely underneath it, maintaining atmospheric pressure below the water sheet.

q: 13. In a depressed nappe ............
options: the pressure below the nappe is atmospheric
the pressure below the nappe is negative
the pressure above the nappe is atmospheric
the pressure above the nappe is negative
explain: In a depressed nappe, air is trapped and partially exhausted by the flowing water, creating a partial vacuum (negative pressure) underneath.

q: 14. The discharge through a siphon spillway is ............
explain: A siphon spillway acts like a large submerged orifice or pipe under a head $H$, where $H$ is the difference between upstream and downstream water levels.

q: 15. The discharge through a channel of rectangular section will be maximum, if ............
options: its depth is twice the breadth
its breadth is twice the depth
its depth is thrice the breadth
its breadth is thrice the depth
explain: For a rectangular channel to be most economical, the hydraulic radius should be half the depth ($R = y/2$), which occurs when the width $b$ is twice the depth $y$ ($b = 2y$).

q: 16. In a venturiflume, the flow takes place at ............
explain: Since a venturiflume is an open channel structure, the water surface is in contact with the atmosphere, so flow occurs at atmospheric pressure.

q: 17. The shape of fire hose nozzle is generally kept ...............
explain: Convergent nozzles are used to increase the velocity of the liquid jet for fire fighting purposes.

q: 18. When water flows over a rectangular suppressed weir, the negative pressure created beneath the nappe ...............
explain: Negative pressure (vacuum) under the nappe sucks the water sheet downwards, increasing the effective head and thereby increasing the discharge.

q: 19. When no air is left below the nappe and water stream adheres to the downstream face of the weir, it is known as ...............
explain: A clinging nappe occurs when the air is exhausted from the space beneath the nappe, causing it to 'cling' to the weir's downstream face.

q: 20. With a clinging nappe of a weir, the excess discharge, is ...............
explain: Because of the lack of ventilation and the resulting vacuum effect, the discharge for a clinging nappe can be significantly higher (up to 25-30%) than a free nappe.

q: 21. A stepped notch is a combination of ...............
explain: A stepped notch consists of multiple rectangular sections of varying widths, used to measure discharge that varies widely over time.

q: 22. The ratio of the percentage error in the discharge and percentage error in the measurement of head, over rectangular notch, is ...............
explain: Since $Q \propto H^{3/2}$ for a rectangular notch, $ rac{dQ}{Q} =  rac{3}{2}  rac{dH}{H}$.

q: 23. Cippoletti weir is a ...............
options: rectangular weir hose length is kept 3 times the height of the water above sill
triangular weir whose notch angle is 90°
trapezoidal weir, whose sides slope 1 horizontal to 4 verticals
a combination of rectangular and triangular weirs
explain: A Cippoletti weir is a trapezoidal weir with side slopes of 1:4 (horizontal to vertical). This specific slope is designed to compensate for the reduction in discharge due to end contractions.

q: 24. The thickness of a sharp crested weir is kept less than ...............
options: one-third of the height of water on the sill
one-half of the height of water on the sill
two-third of the height of water on the sill
explain: To ensure that the water spring (nappe) touches only the upstream edge and stays clear of the crest, the thickness of a sharp-crested weir should be less than half the head of water ($H/2$).

q: 25. Flow of water in pipes of diameter more than 3 meter can be measured by ...............
explain: For very large diameter pipes where installing a venturimeter is impractical/expensive, a Pitot tube is used to measure velocity at various points to determine discharge.

q: 26. The discharge formula Q = Cd √(2gH) × A is used to rectangular ...............
explain: This standard formula assumes the velocity is constant across the area, which is only valid for 'small' orifices where the head is large compared to the orifice depth.

q: 27. Pitot-tube is used for measurement of
explain: A Pitot tube measures the stagnation pressure to determine the local velocity of the fluid at the specific point where the tube is placed.

q: 28. Which mouthpiece is having maximum co-efficient of discharge?
explain: A convergent-divergent mouthpiece minimizes energy loss and prevents flow separation, resulting in a coefficient of discharge that can reach 1.0.

q: 29. Mouthpieces are used to measure
explain: A mouthpiece is a short tube attached to an orifice, also used for measuring the rate of flow or discharge from a tank.

q: 30. The ratio of the area of the jet of water at veena-contracta to the area of orifice is known as
explain: The Coefficient of Contraction (Cc) is the ratio of the area of the jet at the vena contracta to the area of the orifice.

q: 31. Notch is a device used for measuring
options: rate of flow through a small channel
explain: Notches are used to measure the discharge in open channels or small streams, whereas meters like the venturimeter are used for closed pipes.

q: 32. Cipolletti weir is a trapezoidal weir having side slope of
explain: A Cipolletti weir has side slopes of 1 horizontal to 4 vertical (1:4) to compensate for the discharge reduction caused by end contractions.
